mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < 800k) signals weakening aggregate demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST < 800k.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals broad-based supply chain weakness, which erodes earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 2% for three consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and restrictive policy, which increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals improving consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is above its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS month-over-month change > 0.4%) coincident with an unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a high-growth regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS MoM > 0.4% and UNRATE < 4% in a high-growth regime.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 700k for eight consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST remains below 700k for eight consecutive months.
